_notes: Era-band colours for the historical map slider. DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM data/operator-colors.json and never to be merged into it: 'Great Western Railway' the 1923-1947 grouping company and 'GW' the modern TOC are DIFFERENT REAL ENTITIES that share a name, and this repo has already been bitten by exactly that collision (see operators-content.json's _notes on GW's wikipedia_title having pointed at the historic 1833-1947 company). Keying both in one file would make that collision structural. The two files never render simultaneously either — the locked source-switch means the map draws OHM historical lines before 1994 and data/line-segments.json after, so there is no zoom or year at which an era colour and an operator colour appear together. Structure mirrors operator-colors.json (dark/light per entry, light theme as the anchor) so map.html can load and read it with the same helper. CONSTRAINTS FROM CLAUDE.md, all checked: turquoise --t (#40E0D0) is reserved for UI meaning and is used by nothing here (closest is SR malachite: hue 155deg vs turquoise's 174deg, deltaE 32 — measured, not assumed); the literal --a delays/warnings amber (#F5B84B) is not used either. Colours are grounded in each company's real livery rather than picked for contrast alone, then checked for mutual distinguishability — see distinguishability_check below for the measured separations.

pre1923.label: Pre-grouping
pre1923._note: The pre-grouping era had hundreds of independent companies and OHM carries a usable company name for only ~30% of the network, so per-company colouring is not honest at this scale — the band renders one neutral. A parchment/stone neutral rather than a grey: it reads as 'historic' without borrowing the --dim UI ink token (#9AA4B2), which would make map linework look like disabled UI text. Deliberately desaturated toward stone rather than a warm tan — a first pass used #C4A987 and measured only deltaE 22.8 against GWR chocolate, which would have made the 1923 band change nearly invisible across GWR territory (the largest of the four networks). At #C9BBA4 the nearest neighbour in the whole era palette is 32.3.

unknown.label: Company unrecorded
unknown._note: INTENTIONALLY IDENTICAL to this band's own dark/light values. The locked decision makes pre1923 a single neutral band, so co_pre1923 drives the POPUP only and never paint — there is no attributed-vs-unknown colour distinction to make here. The key exists so all three bands expose the same shape to map.html (one lookup path, no per-band special-casing) and so it can be given its own value later if the band ever stops being single-colour. 6,859 of 10,754 pre1923-band features have no company name, and they render exactly like the 3,895 that do.

highlight._note: Neutral band — the hard case flagged in the brief. A "brighter grey" against a grey network would not register, so these are pushed all the way to pure white / pure black. 18.2 in dark is the LOWEST of any band and is a hard ceiling, not a tuning choice: the base #C9BBA4 is already a light stone at L*76, so white is only 24 L* away. The glow is 3.6-7x the line width and blurred, so most of the "this one is selected" signal is the halo itself; the colour only has to say which line it belongs to.

big4.label: The Big Four
big4._note: KNOWN-ONLY colouring per the locked decision. Only lines whose OHM company name resolves through data/big4-constituents.json get a company colour; everything else in the band takes `unknown`. MEASURED: 11.3% of ways alive in this band resolve, so ~89% renders as `unknown`. That is a deliberate honesty trade — no territorial inference — but it means `unknown` must be visually distinct from the pre1923 neutral or the 1923 band change will be nearly invisible on the map. It is: a cool blue-grey (deltaE 32.8) against pre1923's warm stone.

Great Western Railway._note: GWR's Brunswick green locomotive green would collide with both LNER apple green and SR malachite green — three greens in a four-colour band is unusable. The chocolate-and-cream coaching livery is equally real, equally iconic, and the only one of GWR's identities that is not a green.

highlight._note: FLAGGED, BELOW THE BAR: 9.3 dE in LIGHT theme, against a 15 target. Apple green is the one company colour whose light-theme value (#6B8E23) already sits at the contrast floor — its luminance is 0.227 against a 0.253 ceiling for contrast 3.0 on the light basemap — so there is almost no room to go brighter without the highlight becoming less visible than the resting line. Two alternatives were measured and rejected as defaults, both available if Aaron prefers them: #156300 (deep vivid green, dE 19.0, contrast 6.69) clears the bar but goes DARKER, inconsistent with the other three companies, and sits only 12.5 from Southern Railway base; #A48904 (mustard, dE 17.5, contrast 3.06, clears SR by 34.2) clears everything but stops reading as apple green. The shipped value keeps both the direction and the hue identity and clears every band-mate by >= 15 — its weakness is only against its own base.

Southern Railway._note: Pulled deliberately greener/darker than true malachite so it stays clear of the reserved turquoise --t (#40E0D0). Measured hue separation ~22deg plus a large lightness gap.

unknown.label: Company unknown
unknown._note: Not 'no company' — these lines had an owner, we just cannot evidence which one from open sources. The UI should say so rather than implying the line was unowned or unimportant. THIS IS THE ONLY per-band unknown that actually renders: measured 9,280 of 10,465 big4-band features (88.7%) fall here. Its distinctness from the pre1923 band colour is therefore what makes the 1923 transition visible at all for the majority of the map — measured deltaE 32.8 against pre1923 #C9BBA4, and 27.5 against BR rail blue for the 1948 transition. Tune with those two numbers in mind rather than in isolation.

highlight._note: The other neutral. Far more headroom than pre1923 because the blue-grey base is mid-lightness in both themes.

br.label: British Railways
br.livery: BR rail blue (BS 4800 18 E 53 / monastral blue)
br._note: A single nationalised operator needs no lookup, which is why Phase 1's finding that the string 'British Railways' appears exactly once in OHM's entire GB tag set turned out not to matter — co_br is written as a constant. Checked against the modern palette's deep blues (NT #1310C9/#0F0D78, SW #2D4ED0/#24398C): distinct, and in any case they never render at the same slider position.

unknown.label: Company unrecorded
unknown._note: UNREACHABLE IN PRACTICE — present for schema symmetry only. co_br is written as the constant 'British Railways' on every feature alive in 1948-1993, so measured attribution in this band is 10,304/10,304 = 100.0% and this value can never be selected. Kept so map.html's band lookup has a uniform shape; if it ever renders, something upstream has broken and that is worth noticing rather than silently falling back to a company colour.

highlight._note: "A brighter blue in the Rail Blue family" — hue held within ~12deg of BS 4800 18 E 53 in both themes.

modern.label: Present day
modern._note: NO COLOURS HERE BY DESIGN. The modern band renders from data/line-segments.json using data/operator-colors.json, per the locked source-switch at 1994. Duplicating any operator hex into this file would create exactly the two-sources-of-truth problem this file exists to avoid. The upper bound of this band is the CURRENT YEAR resolved at runtime, never a hardcoded literal.

distinguishability_check.method: Pairwise CIE76 deltaE over the dark-theme values, plus explicit hue separation from the reserved turquoise --t (#40E0D0). Run by scripts/build-attribution.mjs --check-palette.
distinguishability_check._note: Measured 2026-07-26: every pair in the era palette is at least deltaE 27.5 apart (closest pair big4/unknown vs br); every entry is at least deltaE 32 from the reserved turquoise. See HISTORICAL-SLIDER-FINDINGS.md Phase 2A.

per_band_unknown._note: Added 2026-07-26 for Phase 2B. Only big4.unknown is reachable; see each band's own unknown._note.

_highlight_notes: 2026-07-27. The colour of the SELECTION GLOW for a highlighted (hovered or click-locked) segment in this band. Was the flat UI accent (--t turquoise) for every band regardless of era; now each band highlights in its own colour family so the highlight reads as "a brighter version of this line" rather than an unrelated UI colour. Values were optimised, not eyeballed: for each one, maximise CIEDE2000 against the band base subject to (a) contrast >= 3.0 against the real Stadia basemap background (#333333 dark, rgb(242,243,240) light — read from the live style JSON, not assumed), (b) never less saturated than the base, and (c) >= 15 dE from every OTHER colour rendered in the same band at the same time. Direction differs by theme because the bases do: dark-theme bases are light-on-dark so highlights go BRIGHTER, and the two neutral bands go to pure white; light-theme bases are dark-on-light so the neutrals go to pure BLACK (near-white would dissolve into the basemap) while the chromatics go brighter and more vivid. See each entry for its measured dE.
